newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW - Jardine welcomes Cheung Kong investment.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Jardine welcomes Cheung Kong investment.

text.p: Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd managing director Alasdair Morrison said on Tuesday he was happy with the Cheung Kong group's recent investment in Jardine Matheson and Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd.

"We are pleased that they recognise good value in Jardine Matheson and Hongkong Land," he told Reuters. Jardine Matheson announced on Tuesday that Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd together held a 3.03 percent stake in Jardine Matheson and a 3.06 percent stake in Hongkong Land as of August 1.
The announcement fuelled speculation that a takeover bid for Hongkong Land could be on the way, analysts said.
Local property developer Cheung Kong, along with several other blue chip companies, made a raid against Hongkong Land, a Hong Kong-based property investor, in September 1987.

Following the October 1987 stock market crash, the raiders sold the shares back to the Jardine group and made a gentlemen's agreement not to attempt another takeover for seven or eight years, anlaysts said.
"We just believe that they bought the shares because they recognise good value in the companies," Morrison said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.

The Jardine group holds about 32 percent of Hongkong Land through Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd, which was set up after the 1987 raid as an investment vehicle to hold the Jardine group's investments in listed companies.
Under the Bermuda takeover code, a company has to disclose shareholdings of three percent or more, Morrison said.
Jardine Matheson moved its domicile to Bermuda from Hong Kong in 1984 when the Sino-British Joint Declaraction was signed setting out the terms of Hong Kong's handover to China on July 1, 1997.
Morrison said he believed the Cheung Kong group had acquired the shares in the market. He also said the Jardine group was happy to cooperate with Cheung Kong, Hutchison and other companies.

"As a group, we have a couple of areas where we are co-investors with Hutchison. We are both shareholders in the river trade terminal and in HAECO, so we are always happy to join ventures and cooperate with a number of different companies," he added.
